title: Audit generator banks and usable fuel
lead: The original startup lessons ask whether a generator becomes available in time. This lesson asks a different question: can the available bank carry the backed load at all? Follow a source claim through its real-power conversion, post-loss capacity and fuel ledger. A failed arithmetic claim should stay failed even when the combined installed nameplates look impressive.
objectives: Convert the source-specific generator kVA rating to real-power capability.
Test one independent bank after one unit is unavailable.
Separate usable fuel consumption from gross tank volume and dynamic qualification.

sections.title: Define what is backed
sections.body: The backed load may include IT, cooling needed for continuity, controls, fans, pumps, fuel transfer and permitted recharge. Essential demand is a declared classification, not another name for IT alone. The manuscript’s project claims that either generator bank supports the complete 27 MW facility. Each source unit is 3,000 kVA at a stated rated power factor of 0.8, or 2.4 MW under that rating relationship.

sections.title: Reject the incorrect inequality
sections.body: A ten-unit bank with one unavailable unit provides 9 × 2.4 = 21.6 MW, which is below 27 MW by 5.4 MW. Even ten healthy units provide only 24 MW. With no derating or loading ceiling, the elementary N+1 screen requires thirteen installed units per independent bank; twelve remain and provide 28.8 MW. With both factors at 0.9, fifteen installed units are required. Neither change constitutes an approved redesign.

sections.title: Follow fuel and time separately
sections.body: At a constant 27,000 kW for 48 hours and an assumed source coefficient of 0.25 L/kWh, usable consumption is 324,000 L. Gross storage, reserve, inaccessible volume, quality, transfer pumps and replenishment are separate questions. A steady capacity total also does not establish startup, load-step acceptance, synchronizing, qualification or restoration. The transition storyboard is explanatory; it must not emit real closing commands or invented synchronization limits.

challenge.question: Does thirteen installed per side close the capacity screen?
challenge.answer: Twelve remain, giving 28.8 MW and 1.8 MW headroom. Dynamic, routing, fuel, emissions and equipment evidence remain open.

instructions: Read the declared boundary and units. Predict the selected result before calculating.
Run the starting case and inspect the ledger, assumptions and model limits.
Apply the challenge, run again, and explain the difference. Export only the last completed inputs and results.

scene.title: The generator bank that cannot meet its claim
storyboard: Expose ten labelled generator blocks per bank.
Remove one and compare 21.6 MW with the 27 MW demand plane.
Add units through the capacity-only control without erasing the open redesign badge.
Trace bulk tank → transfer pump → day tank separately from the electrical route.
scene.interaction: Change installed units and derating; inspect a separate fuel calculation and an illustrative start/qualify/load sequence.
scene.staticAlternative: Per-bank surviving-unit table, capacity inequality and usable-fuel ledger.
scene.projection: orthographic axonometric SVG with upright HTML labels
scene.timelineSemantics: Narrative steps unless an explicitly labelled physical-time model is active.

assessments.question: Find usable fuel for 8 MW over 36 h at 0.27 L/kWh.
assessments.answer: 77,760 L before gross-volume and operational allowances.
assessments.rubric: Convert MW to kW and preserve L/kWh.

assessments.question: Find the N+1 count for 27 MW with 2.4 MW units, derating 0.95 and loading 0.9.
assessments.answer: 2.052 MW usable per unit; fourteen operating plus one spare = fifteen installed per bank.
assessments.rubric: Round up the required operating count.

assessments.question: Why does a no-load engine run not prove a whole-facility transfer?
assessments.answer: It does not demonstrate load acceptance, transfer equipment, sustained fuel supply, cooling recovery or service continuity.
assessments.rubric: List dependencies outside the engine-only test.

limits: Capacity-only redesign screens; no approved generator selection or operational switching procedure.
Fuel coefficient is fixed and source-specific; variable-load consumption requires integration.
